title: Concrete finite-reduction square for the compactification projection mate
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$; put $A_n=R/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], not a datum assuming projection invertibility. Schemes are finite type over $k$ and their structure morphisms need not be separated. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified compactification projection map [def-exchange-projection], with compact-support functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, $1\le m\le n$, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$, where finite Tor amplitude is [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $\rho_W(M)=M\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$, $K_m=\rho_XK$, $L_m=\rho_YL$. Write $S_n=Rf_{!,n}K\otimes^L L$ and $T_n=Rf_{!,n}(K\otimes^LLf_n^*L)$, and similarly $S_m,T_m$. The pullback and tensor input $K\otimes^LLf_n^*L$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude: if the input Tor intervals are $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, its interval is $[a+c,b+d]$. The canonical tensor and compact-support comparisons give isomorphisms $u:\rho_YS_n\xrightarrow{\sim}S_m$ and $v:\rho_YT_n\xrightarrow{\sim}T_m$ with
$$v\,\rho_Y(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L})=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}\,u.$$
Here $u$ first uses tensor comparison, then compact-support comparison; $v$ first uses compact-support comparison, then tensor and pullback comparisons. This identifies the actual proper counit/open tensor composite for every chosen compactification, naturally in both inputs and compatibly with successive reductions; it asserts no invertibility of PF.

proof.text: Pullback preserves the finite Tor interval by lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude. Apply lem-sf-tensor-ctf on flat K-flat resolutions and transport along the selected tensor-model representative isomorphism. This proves finite Tor constructibility of the actual input functor and the sum interval.

The concrete support quotient comparison is invertible on K and on the tensor/pullback input by lem-sf-concrete-support-scalar-isomorphism. Tensor and pullback comparisons are isomorphisms by their definitions, so u and v are isomorphisms. No projection is inverted.

Expand the specified projection using its unique proper/open projection data. Its proper factor is the counit-defined properProjection; the open factor is openFactor including the geometric pullback compositor. The support comparison factors as properScalar followed by the proper image of openScalar, by the canonical mate factorization, with the intermediate scalar presentation isomorphisms cancelling.

Naturality of properScalar at the open projection moves scalar change across the open map. Substitute lem-sf-concrete-open-scalar-tensor-square and lem-sf-concrete-proper-scalar-tensor-square. Naturality of the B proper projection at openScalar K moves the last factor to the source, where tensor functoriality combines it with properScalar. The result is exactly scalar(projection_A);v = u;projection_B.

Assemble the source, input and target comparison natural transformations from whiskering and products. Their naturality gives naturality in both inputs. Uncurry the specified projection natural transformation to obtain projection naturality.

Use the tensor, support and input comparison composition and identity equations of lem-sf-concrete-projection-coefficient-coherence. Naturality and tensor/support functoriality combine the component equations into the two endpoint cocycles and identity equations. These are exactly Composition and Identity for each finite quotient, with no hypothesis on the separatedness of structure maps.

theorem concreteProjectionReductionSquare
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (C : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (_operations : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) :
    ∀ (m₀ : Models.{u}) (choices₀ : Choices m₀)
      (X Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)))
      [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
      [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom]
      (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.left] [QuasiCompact f.left]
      (cpt : Compactification f.left)
      (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory X.left (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n))
      (L : proEtaleDerivedCategory Y.left (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n)),
      finiteTorConstructible C.l E n hn X.left K →
      finiteTorConstructible C.l E n hn Y.left L →
      (∀ a b c d : ℤ,
        HasProEtaleTorAmplitude X.left (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n) K a b →
        HasProEtaleTorAmplitude Y.left (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n) L c d →
        finiteTorConstructible C.l E n hn X.left
          (input m₀ (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n) f.left K L) ∧
        HasProEtaleTorAmplitude X.left (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n)
          (input m₀ (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n) f.left K L) (a + c) (b + d)) ∧
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (_hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ n),
        Square m₀ choices₀ (quotient C.l E hmn) cpt K L ∧
        Naturality m₀ choices₀ (quotient C.l E hmn) cpt ∧
        ∀ (r : ℕ) (_hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrm : r ≤ m),
          Composition m₀ choices₀ (quotient C.l E hmn) (quotient C.l E hrm) cpt K L) ∧
      Identity m₀ choices₀ (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n) cpt K L
